bills.title: Relating to elections; and declaring an emergency.
In memoriam: State Senator Aaron Lionel Woods.

reading.body:
Oregon had six bills touching AI-adjacent subjects active in its 2026 legislative session, covering a range from AI companions to elections to journalism compensation, with no single dominant theme.

The bills cluster in early-to-mid 2026, between March and April. Only two carry "artificial intelligence" explicitly in their titles, HB4103 and SB1546. The others address areas where AI is implicated indirectly: election integrity, automated medical billing adjustments described as downcoding, and compensation frameworks for journalism in an AI-scraped media environment. SCR206 is a memorial resolution and is not substantive legislation.

None of these bills address compute infrastructure, data center siting, energy consumption, or grid access. That absence is a fact worth noting. Oregon hosts significant data center capacity, but this legislative snapshot does not reflect that physical and electrical reality. What the data covers is the consumer-facing and media-facing layer of AI policy, which is one slice of the regulatory picture, not the whole of it.
